test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 04 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: A spherical chocolate truffle with radius 6 cm has a spherical hollow cavity at its centre. If the volume of chocolate used is exactly 800π/3 cm³, what is the radius of the hollow cavity (rounded off to two decimal places)?
solution:
**Given:**

Outer radius = 6

Volume of chocolate = 800π ÷ 3

**Formula Used:**

Volume of sphere = (4 ÷ 3)πr³

Volume of hollow = Outer volume − Inner volume

**Calculation:**

⇒ Outer volume = (4 ÷ 3)π × 6³

⇒ Outer volume = (4 ÷ 3)π × 216

⇒ Outer volume = 288π

⇒ Chocolate volume = Outer − Inner

⇒ 288π − (4 ÷ 3)πr³ = 800π ÷ 3

⇒ Multiply by 3

⇒ 864π − 4πr³ = 800π

⇒ 864π − 800π = 4πr³

⇒ 64π = 4πr³

⇒ r³ = 16

⇒ r = ∛16

⇒ r ≈ 2.52

**∴ The correct answer is 2.52.**
